scenes.headline: distinct()
scenes.subtitle: Removing duplicate rows from a DataFrame.
scenes.narration: The distinct transformation returns only the unique rows, removing exact duplicates across all columns.

scenes.headline: What distinct does
items: Keeps only unique rows across all columns
dropDuplicates lets you dedupe on a subset of columns
Requires a shuffle to compare rows across partitions
Can be expensive on very large datasets
scenes.narration: Distinct keeps only unique rows across all columns, while dropDuplicates lets you dedupe on a chosen subset. It requires a shuffle to compare rows across partitions, so it can be expensive on very large datasets.

scenes.headline: Distinct vs dropDuplicates
scenes.code:
unique_events = events_df.distinct()

# Dedupe on specific keys only
one_per_user = events_df.dropDuplicates(["user_id"])
scenes.narration: Calling distinct returns fully unique rows across every column. In contrast, dropDuplicates with a key list keeps just one row per user id, which is useful when only certain columns define uniqueness.

scenes.text: distinct triggers a shuffle — filter first to shrink the data before deduping.
scenes.narration: Because distinct triggers a shuffle, filter the data down first so Spark has fewer rows to compare and move.
